primary_root_cause: Weak, undercharged, or failing battery unable to hold voltage above 12.2V at idle
other_likely_causes: Faulty or underperforming charging system (stator/alternator or voltage regulator not raising output above idle level as RPM increases)
Corroded, loose, or high-resistance battery cable/ground connections
Parasitic electrical draw from accessories draining battery faster than charging system replenishes it
Failed or degraded voltage regulator rectifier not properly regulating charging voltage
recommended_first_check: Load-test the battery and measure static/cranking voltage; if battery is good, check charging system output (stator AC voltage and regulated DC voltage at battery) at idle and at 2000+ RPM
reasoning: P0562 is triggered purely on measured voltage thresholds, so the most common and easiest-to-rule-out cause is a weak or aged battery, followed by a charging system that fails to boost voltage as RPM rises. Corroded connections and grounds are also frequent culprits since they cause voltage drop independent of battery or stator health. Urgency is medium because the bike will likely still run in the short term but risks a no-start or stall if charging voltage continues to sag, especially at night with lights/accessories loading the system.
